THF (tetrahydrofuran) and ethyl ether (diethyl ether) are both common laboratory solvents that share a particular hazardous property. While they are indeed flammable (option A) and can potentially penetrate skin (option C), their most distinctive hazard is their ability to form explosive peroxides when exposed to air over time.

These ethers can react with oxygen in the air to form unstable peroxide compounds, which can accumulate, especially in older bottles or containers that have been opened multiple times. These peroxides can be shock-sensitive and potentially explosive, especially when concentrated during evaporation or distillation processes. This is why laboratories have special protocols for handling, storing, and disposing of these solvents, including regular testing for peroxide formation and dating bottles upon opening.
